statement: On ResearchClawBench end-to-end scientific re-discovery, the best autonomous agent (Claude Code 21.5) barely exceeds the best harnessed single LLM (Claude-Opus-4.7 20.7); both remain far below the 50-point target-paper level.
uncertainty: ResearchHarness gives LLMs tools (not pure single-prompt); agent vs harnessed-LLM gap is small

statement: Under matched thinking-token budgets on multi-hop reasoning (FRAMES, MuSiQue), single-agent systems consistently match or outperform multi-agent architectures across three model families; reported MAS gains often reflect unaccounted compute.
uncertainty: Tasks are multi-hop QA, not full scientific research pipelines; MAS can help under severe context degradation

statement: PaperQA2 agentic RAG significantly beats a non-agentic fixed pipeline on LitQA2 (p=0.015); agent can revise searches. PaperQA2 also exceeds PhD/postdoc precision on literature QA and produces more accurate Wikipedia-style gene summaries than Wikipedia.
uncertainty: Baseline is non-agentic RAG / humans / commercial RAG, not a maximally prompted single model with identical tools and token budget

statement: Arbor hypothesis-tree research agent beats Codex and Claude Code on six autonomous optimization research tasks (>2.5x average relative held-out gain) under same interface and resource budget; also leads MLE-Bench Lite with GPT-5.5 (86.36% Any Medal).
uncertainty: Baselines are coding agents, not a single well-prompted chat model; living technical report

statement: Anthropic reports multi-agent research outperforms single-agent Opus 4 by 90.2% on an internal research eval for breadth-first queries, but also that token usage alone explains 80% of BrowseComp variance and multi-agent uses ~15x more tokens than chat.
uncertainty: Internal eval not public; outperformance may largely be compute scaling rather than coordination architecture

statement: STORM multi-agent with shared-state management outperforms single-agent on PaperBench Code-Dev (74.1 vs 68.7 Sonnet) and Commit0; combined single+multi best, showing complementarity.
uncertainty: PaperBench Code-Dev is research-code reproduction, not open discovery; single-agent cheaper

statement: On ScienceAgentBench scientific coding tasks, a simple self-debug agent nearly doubles Claude-3.5-Sonnet success vs direct prompting (16.7%→32.4%) and beats the heavier OpenHands agent at far lower cost—showing interactive agent loops help vs one-shot prompts, but complex multi-agent frameworks are not automatically better.
uncertainty: Self-debug is a single-model iterative agent, not a multi-agent research system; still far from solving most tasks (≤34.3%)

statement: Controlled multi-benchmark study (260 configs) finds MAS gains are not universal: capability saturation (~45% SAS baseline) predicts zero/negative gains; performance vs SAS ranges from +80.8% to −70%; Anthropic similarly attributes much BrowseComp variance to tokens.
uncertainty: Benchmarks include software/finance/planning more than open-ended scientific discovery

statement: PaperQA2 exceeds PhD/postdoc precision on LitQA2 literature QA and produces Wikipedia-style summaries with fewer unsupported citations than human Wikipedia articles—human-expert evidence for agent research quality, but vs humans not vs a matched single well-prompted model.
uncertainty: Does not isolate autonomy vs a single model given identical tools and token budget

statement: Challenge (P1/P3/P4): Positive agent claims often assume unmatched compute/tools (Anthropic 15× tokens; ResearchHarness tools for LLMs). Contradicts naive outperformance narrative: ResearchClawBench near-parity; matched-budget SAS≥MAS. Goal coverage gap: few studies compare autonomous research agents to a single well-prompted model with equal tools and tokens on open-ended discovery.
uncertainty: Sequential adversarial pass in one context, not independent reviewers
